subject: Staged GPU add + safety-net proposal for Aperture Health renewal
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@aperturehealth.com>, Aperture Health Procurement <procurement@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged GPU add + safety-net proposal for Aperture Health renewal

Hi Elena / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the sync this morning — appreciate the transparency on the spike you saw over the last two weeks. Per our conversation, I ran a sizing pass based on the trailing 90-day utilization and the burst profiles you shared. Two high-level options that keep reliability during the renewal window while minimizing long-term commit risk:

1) Immediate safety-net + staged conversion (recommended)
   - Add 4 H100s to your dedicated pool immediately (safety-net). These will be hot-standby for spikes and used for low-latency / high-QPS short prompts.
   - Convert up to 10 additional GPUs (H100 equiv) over an 8-week window if 7-day rolling utilization stays above 68% and average request latency requirement is met.
   - Keep a 2-GPU hot fallback in a cross-region pool for failover.

2) Aggressive upsize (higher commitment)
   - Add 12 GPUs now to eliminate risk of throttling at peak — higher commit and cost.

Recommendations rationale:
- Your 90-day median utilization sits at ~46% but 95th percentile spikes to ~210% of the median during batch-promotion hours. A small immediate add plus staged conversion smooths spend and gives us signal to convert more GPUs only if needed.
- We can enable KV-prefix caching for commonly repeated prefixes and a lightweight quantization profile for the model family you run to shave ~15% per-token cost while keeping QA stable.

Commercials & next steps:
- Attached: draft SOW and a sizing workbook that shows monthly cost scenarios for each path (Aperture_GPU_Sizing_v3.xlsx).
- If you want to move faster we can sign the SOW and schedule a 30-day SLA trial for the immediate safety-net. I can propose a promotional 10% credit on the first month to cover onboarding burst.

Action items for Aperture:
- Confirm whether Procurement prefers the staged route or the immediate upsize.
- If staged: confirm the 8-week conversion window and acceptance criteria (I suggest 7-day rolling utilization > 68% and no latency regressions > 95th pct SLO).

Happy to jump back on a call tomorrow to walk through the workbook live.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Staged GPU add + safety-net proposal for Aperture Health renewal

Hi Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the workbook. A few clarifying questions before Procurement greenlights anything: 

- Pricing: can you break out the incremental cost for the 4-GPU safety-net vs the 12-GPU immediate upsize (monthly and one-time onboarding)? Procurement wants a clear delta.
- SLA: our product team needs confirmation on 95th percentile latency for short-form prompts ( < 512 tokens ) under the safety-net configuration. If you can put a latency SLO in the SOW for that workload that helps us a lot.
- Trial: the 30-day trial sounds good — we want the ability to revert the staged conversion if it materially impacts latency or cost beyond the thresholds. How will rollback be handled operationally?

We also noticed that the spike coincided with a release we did two weeks ago; the spike happened in region us-west-2 and had short (~150ms) avg latency requirements. If the safety-net keeps latency < 200ms p95 for these short prompts, product is comfortable moving forward.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of ML Platform, Aperture Health
elena@aperturehealth.com

Subject: Fwd: Re: Staged GPU add + safety-net proposal for Aperture Health renewal

Team — forwarding Elena's note and the workbook. Quick ask: can we approve a modest commercial concession and an SLA carve for the 30-day trial so we don't lose the deal during procurement? My suggested concession: 10% credit on month 1 consumption for onboarding and a temporary SLO addendum limited to the trial window (p95 < 200ms for <512 token short prompts on the 4-GPU safety-net in us-west-2).

I propose we slightly hedge the risk operationally by:
- Starting with only 4 immediate H100s (safety-net) instead of 8. If utilization signals justify it, we convert more.
- Activating a canary routing policy that directs 5% of production traffic to the new safety-net pool for 72 hours before ramping to 25%, with automated rollback if p95 latency or error rate exceed thresholds.

Impact: reduces near-term commit and limits exposure if their recent release causes sustained demand. Win for both sides.

Approvals needed:
- Kimberly: confirm pricing flexibility and whether 10% one-time credit is okay for a promotional onboarding concession.
- Rishi: confirm that the temporary SLA addendum is acceptable from a risk perspective and that ops can run the canary and rollback plan.
- Marissa: confirm CS readiness to run the onboarding checklist and the 72-hour canary monitoring.

If I don't hear objections by EOD I'll send the updated SOW and a DocuSign link to Aperture.

—Ben

Hi Elena / Procurement —

Following internal alignment, attached is an updated SOW and a condensed commercial note:

Summary of what we can do now (no change to trial scope):
- Immediate: provision 4 H100-equivalent GPUs in us-west-2 as a safety-net pool.
- Canary: route 5% traffic to the pool for 72 hours, then 25% for 7 days if p95 < 200ms and error rate < 0.5%.
- Conversion trigger: convert an additional 6 GPUs over 4 weeks if 7-day rolling utilization > 68% and no sustained p95 regressions.
- Fallback: cross-region 2-GPU cold-standby for emergency failover (separate charge only if used).

Commercials (high level):
- Safety-net add: incremental $28,400 / month (4x H100-equivalent units)
- Conversion tranche (6 GPUs): incremental $42,600 / month when triggered
- One-time onboarding & migration: $7,500 (includes canary setup, routing policy, and CS-run checklist)
- Promotional concession: 10% credit applied to first month of consumption after sign (one-time).
